title: Double consonants
short_explanation: Some common words need doubled letters. Learn the whole visual pattern instead of relying only on sound.
mnemonic: Tomorrow has a double r; useful has one l.

title: Vowel order: i and e
short_explanation: The order of i and e changes the spelling of a word. After c, most words use ei.

title: Lose vs loose
short_explanation: Lose is a verb meaning to not have something anymore. Loose is an adjective meaning not tight.
mnemonic: One O in lose, like losing one letter.

title: Plural: y becomes ies
short_explanation: When a noun ends in a consonant plus y, change y to i and add es to form the plural.
mnemonic: Company to companies; one lonely y turns into two i's.

title: Irregular past: go / went
short_explanation: Go does not take -ed in the past tense. Its past form is the irregular word went.
mnemonic: Go, went, gone — learn the whole set together.
